conflict_topics: Coverage of Agent D's analysis section before the Thursday deadline
Whether Agent D should work during bereavement vs. the team covering the work
dialogue_quality_notes: Opening exchanges are natural expressions of condolence followed by practical problem-solving.
B and C give brief, grounded reasons for inability to help (capacity and skills), which informs A's choice.
Agent A's repeated, explicit commitment ('I'll do it') functions as clear leadership and closure.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A (the lead) took responsibility for completing Agent D's section and Agent D agreed to provide what they had. Key lines: Agent A: "I'll do it, Agent D. Really. It's my responsibility as the lead to make sure it gets done." (Turn 12). Agent D: "Thank you, Agent A. I'll send you everything I've done so far." (Turn 13). B and C had stated they could not help (Turns 4 and 5).
position_change_notes: Agent A shifted from condolence and planning to explicitly accepting responsibility for D's section (Turns 3, 7, 9, 12).
Agent D moved from offering to continue working remotely (Turn 6) to accepting the team's accommodation and providing files (Turn 13), softening their initial offer to work.
Agents B and C retained their positions of inability to take on additional work (Turns 4 and 5).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A expresses sympathy (Turn 1). Agent D states the wake lasts two days and he must be there (Turn 2). No incompatible claims about work appear in this round.

Agent A notes timing is difficult and that a plan for D's section is needed (Turn 3). Agent B says they are already covering for David and their plate is full (Turn 4). This creates a mild substantive conflict about who can cover the work.

Agent C says they also cannot help and lacks skills (Turn 5). Agent D offers to work from home late at night and to send what they have (Turn 6). Multiple team members declare inability to cover while D offers to continue working, increasing the disagreement about coverage versus D attending the wake.

Agent A insists D should not work and that the team will take care of the section (Turn 7). Agent D replies with concern about who will do it given B and C said they can't (Turn 8). A's offer reduces escalation, but a substantive uncertainty about who will actually produce the section remains.

Agent A repeatedly commits to do the work herself and frames it as her responsibility as lead (Turns 9 and 12). A concrete offer is made, reducing but not yet fully resolving the prior disagreement because the affected parties have not all explicitly accepted it in this round.
Agent D thanks Agent A and says they will send everything they've done so far (Turn 13). This affirms Agent A's takeover and D's acceptance of that arrangement.
Agent D expresses thanks/confirmation again (Turns 18 and 22). No substantive disagreement is present.

substantive_insights: Conflict centered on the tension between an individual's bereavement needs and the team's fixed deadline.
Role responsibility (A as lead) and concrete constraints (B's full plate, C's lack of skills) shaped the available solutions.
The settlement combined a redistribution of labor (A taking the section) and a small cooperative act by D (sending existing work).
